deep_analysis.executive_intro:
This FTSE screen is broadly neutral-to-cautious: 147 names sit on Hold versus 62 actionable Buys (16 Strong Buy, 46 Buy) and 40 Avoids, so value signals are selective rather than market-wide. The five top-ranked Strong Buys all pass every model family (cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP, risk) with full 20/20 data quality, but conviction scores are modest (49–55%) and every signal is new (one week at signal), which limits timing confidence. Sector clustering is visible among leaders: three of five top picks are Industrials (FGP.L, MEGP.L, MGNS.L), with HIK.L in Healthcare and ITV.L in Communication Services. A key data limitation is that NCAV/balance-sheet depth is missing for all top candidates (Graham Net-Net fails universally), and several names show tension between headline value metrics and balance-sheet or cash-flow quality flags that the screen surfaces but does not fully reconcile.

FGP.L (FirstGroup plc) — Industrials. Eleven of 22 models pass (composite 91%, sector-relative 85%), led by Earnings Yield (E/P 10.8%, P/E 9.3), FCF Yield (30.9%), Low P/E + High Yield, Neff PEGY, Magic Formula, Acquirer's Multiple, Dreman Contrarian, Piotroski F-Score (8/9), Composite Value, and Earnings Quality; key metrics are P/E 9.3, P/B 1.4, yield 3.9%, ROE 16.7%. Failures include Financial Health (debt/equity 160.8%, current ratio 0.73), Graham Enterprising (excessive leverage, earnings growth −5.9%), Buffett Quality, and Economic Moat. Industrials concentration adds sector correlation with MEGP.L and MGNS.L. Verdict: watchlist — exceptional headline cheapness and cash generation, but leverage and liquidity failures warrant balance-sheet diligence before sizing.

HIK.L (Hikma Pharmaceuticals) — Healthcare. Thirteen of 22 models pass (composite 81%, sector-relative 91%), including Graham Enterprising, Earnings Yield, Low P/E + High Yield, Lynch PEG (growth 23.5%), Quality Value, Buffett Quality, Dividend Growth, Magic Formula, Acquirer's Multiple, Dreman Contrarian, Composite Value, and Financial Health; metrics are P/E 11.7, P/B 1.8, yield 3.9%, ROE 16.5%, D/E 62%. Notable failures: FCF Yield (3.6% vs 5% threshold), Piotroski F-Score (6/9), Earnings Quality (weak free-cash conversion), and Economic Moat; the cash-conversion overlay downgrades the adjusted signal from Strong Buy to Buy. Verdict: watchlist — attractive GARP and quality pass rate, but FCF conversion weakness and mixed Piotroski score argue for confirmation before accumulation.

MEGP.L (ME Group International) — Industrials. Fifteen of 22 models pass (composite 83%, sector-relative 87%), the broadest pass set among top names, including Graham Enterprising, Earnings Yield, FCF Yield (5.7%), Low P/E + High Yield, Quality Value, Buffett Quality, Economic Moat, High Dividend Yield (7.6%), Magic Formula, Acquirer's Multiple, Dreman Contrarian, and Financial Health; metrics are P/E 7.9, P/B 2.2, yield 7.6%, ROE 28.2%, D/E 28%. Failures include Lynch PEG and Piotroski F-Score (6/9) on earnings growth −3.9% and weak free-cash conversion. Shares the Industrials cluster with FGP.L and MGNS.L. Verdict: accumulate — lowest P/E, highest ROE and yield in the group, strong moat and health passes, with manageable leverage; size with awareness of earnings decline and cash-conversion flags.

ITV.L (ITV plc) — Communication Services. Fourteen of 22 models pass (composite 75%, sector-relative 86%), including Graham Enterprising, Earnings Yield, FCF Yield (5.4%), Lynch PEG (growth 26.7%), Neff PEGY, Quality Value, High Dividend Yield (6.7%), Dividend Growth, Magic Formula, Acquirer's Multiple, Dreman Contrarian, Composite Value, Earnings Quality, and Financial Health; metrics are P/E 12.2, P/B 1.5, yield 6.7%, ROE 13.5%, D/E 52%. Critical failures: Piotroski F-Score 3/9 (ROA, OCF/NI, leverage, margins, and turnover all deteriorating), Buffett Quality, and Economic Moat; operating cash flow fell from $333M to $202M year-on-year per filing-aligned data. Verdict: watchlist — dividend and value screens align, but the weakest financial-trend score in the top five argues against aggressive accumulation until trend stabilizes.

MGNS.L (Morgan Sindall Group) — Industrials. Sixteen of 22 models pass (composite 78%, sector-relative 80%), the highest model count in the cohort, including Graham Enterprising, Earnings Yield, FCF Yield (6.9%), Low P/E + High Yield, Lynch PEG (growth 18.8%), Quality Value, Buffett Quality, Piotroski F-Score (8/9), Magic Formula, Acquirer's Multiple, Dreman Contrarian, Composite Value, Earnings Quality, and Financial Health; metrics are P/E 11.4, P/B 2.6, yield 3.7%, ROE 26.1%, D/E 18%. Failures are mainly deep-value criteria (P/B not below 1.0) and Economic Moat (ROA and margins below thresholds). Third Industrials name alongside FGP.L and MEGP.L. Verdict: accumulate — strongest combined model breadth and Piotroski score with conservative leverage (D/E 18%) and solid FCF yield, suitable for phased entry on the screen's limit levels.

- FGP.L: High leverage (D/E 160.8%) and weak liquidity (current ratio 0.73) are quantitatively flagged but franchise/regulatory risk in UK public transport and potential pension obligations are not captured — open question on defined-benefit exposure and contract renewal.
- FGP.L: Negative earnings growth (−5.9%) alongside thin margins (Buffett Quality, Quality Value failures) suggests cyclical or operational pressure not fully explained by the screen.
- HIK.L: Generic-drug and injectables businesses face patent-cliff and pricing/regulatory risk; the screen does not assess pipeline concentration or FDA/EMA action exposure.
- HIK.L: FCF data is inconsistent (filing-aligned FCF $119M vs screen TTM −$66.1M); dividend sustainability with FCF yield 3.6% and weak earnings quality is an open question.
- MEGP.L: Photo-booth/vending-style Industrials model may face technology disruption and location-contract renewal risk; governance and customer concentration are not screened.
- MEGP.L: 7.6% yield with earnings growth −3.9% and weak free-cash conversion raises dividend-cut risk not resolved by quantitative filters alone.
- ITV.L: Structural decline in linear advertising and streaming competition are qualitative headwinds; Piotroski 3/9 and OCF decline ($333M → $202M) signal deteriorating fundamentals the value screen may lag.
- ITV.L: 6.7% yield may embed market skepticism on payout sustainability — governance and content-investment strategy not assessed.
- MGNS.L: UK construction and contracting is highly cyclical; order-book quality, project margin risk, and fixed-price contract exposure are outside the screen.
- MGNS.L: Economic Moat failure (ROA below 8%, margins below 12%) hints at commoditized contracting economics despite strong ROE — open question on margin durability through a downturn.

- HIK.L — Which FCF figure is authoritative (filing-aligned $119M vs screen TTM −$66.1M), and is the 3.9% dividend safe given weak free-cash conversion and the Buy downgrade on the cash-conversion overlay?

documents.name: FirstGroup plc
documents.executive_summary:
FirstGroup is a UK-focused public transport operator (First Bus ~78% of adjusted revenue; First Rail ~22%) trading on low multiples with strong reported cash generation and an active capital-return programme. The quantitative screen rates the name a **strong buy** (11/22 models, 91% composite), driven by earnings yield, FCF yield, dividend growth, and Piotroski F-Score 8/9. Primary filings show adjusted operating profit rising from £204.3m (FY2024) to £222.8m (FY2025) and adjusted EPS from 16.7p to 19.4p, but adjusted net cash of £64.1m flipped to adjusted net debt of £86.9m as growth capex and the RATP London acquisition absorbed cash. The central debate is whether cheap headline metrics and contract wins (notably ~£3bn London Overground from May 2026) outweigh UK bus/rail policy transition, lease-adjusted leverage, and thin liquidity ratios that several quality screens fail.

---
documents.investment_thesis:
For a value investor, FirstGroup offers a rare combination of **statutory-scale cash businesses** (FY2025 statutory revenue £5.1bn per RNS) with **screen-level cheapness**: P/E 9.3, P/B 1.4, earnings yield 10.8%, FCF yield ~31% (screen TTM), and dividend yield 3.9%. Five factor families pass—cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP, and risk—supported by improving operational trends in filings: adjusted revenue up 17% to £1,370.0m and adjusted operating margin stable at ~16.3% (FY2025 annual report).

Business quality is better than pure cyclical transport: DfT rail contracts carry limited revenue risk; open access (Lumo, Hull Trains) and Additional services add higher-margin growth; First Bus is scaling adjacent services and decarbonisation with government co-funding. Management has returned capital consistently (~£92m buybacks in FY2025; ongoing programmes per news) while targeting at least flat adjusted EPS in FY2026 off a diversified base. The screen’s strong-buy signal aligns with a post-North-America-exit, UK-pure-play operator generating cash through operational improvement rather than financial engineering—though failed Graham, moat, and financial-health models flag leverage and liquidity as offsets to the value case.

documents.name: Hikma Pharmaceuticals PLC
documents.executive_summary: Hikma is a FTSE 100 generic and specialty pharmaceutical group with three engines — US/MENA/Europe Injectables, MENA Branded, and North American Hikma Rx — trading on low double-digit earnings multiples with a ~3.9% yield and active capital returns. FY2025 delivered 6% core revenue growth and 3% core operating profit growth to $741m, but reported operating profit fell 11% after a sodium oxybate antitrust settlement, and management has withdrawn medium-term margin guidance while guiding Injectables margins down to 27–28% in 2026. The value case rests on durable Branded momentum, a refocused Hikma Rx franchise, BBB-rated balance sheet strength, and a $250m buyback plus 5% dividend increase; the key debate is whether Injectables margin compression and weak statutory cash conversion are cyclical mix effects or a structural reset after November 2025’s guidance revision.
documents.investment_thesis:
The quantitative screen flags Hikma as a strong buy across five families — cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP, and risk — with full data quality (20/20 metrics) and sector-leading relative score (91%). At P/E 11.7, P/B 1.8, ROE 16.5%, debt/equity 62%, and 3.9% yield, the name passes classic value screens (Graham Enterprising, Earnings Yield, Low P/E + High Yield, Lynch/Neff PEG, Magic Formula, Acquirer’s Multiple, Dreman Contrarian, Composite Value, Financial Health). That cheapness is not purely mechanical: filings show core EBITDA of $853m (+4%), return on average invested capital of 16.0%, and investment-grade ratings (S&P and Fitch BBB/stable, per FY2025 results release).

Business quality is bifurcated in a way screens only partly capture. Branded grew core revenue 10% with core operating margin expanding to 26.4%; Hikma Rx held ~$1bn revenue with margin ahead of plan at 17.3%. Injectables remains the profit pool but is under pressure: core operating margin fell from 35.3% to 31.0% on US competition, Xellia mix dilution, euro strength, and inventory provisions. For a value investor, the hook is a cash-generative, geographically diversified generics platform trading below peer multiples while returning capital (84c total dividend, +5%; $250m 2026 buyback) — with the screen’s cash-conversion overlay (FCF yield 3.6% vs 5% hurdle; filing-aligned FCF $119m) already tempering the headline signal to adjusted Buy.

documents.name: ME Group International plc
documents.executive_summary: ME Group International plc operates a global estate of ~49,000 automated vending units (photobooths, laundry, ancillary services) across 16 countries, with laundry now the primary growth engine. The quantitative screen rates the name a **strong buy** (15/22 models, composite 83%), anchored on low trailing multiples (P/E 7.9, yield 7.6%, ROE 28.2%, D/E 28%) and solid dividend/cash-generation history. FY2025 (Oct-25 year-end) delivered record profit before tax of **£78.2m** on revenue of **£315.4m**, but H1 FY2026 showed a **3.8% PBT decline** to **£32.7m** after an April consumer slowdown in France, and management has **revised FY2026 PBT guidance to £69–74m** — a step down from the prior-year record. The central debate is whether laundry rollout, contract renewals (SNCF, RATP, Asda), and an **£18m buyback** offset photobooth/regulatory headwinds (Germany ID rules), FX, and governance concerns (late annual report/listing suspension, family-dominated board, January 2026 secondary placing). Valuation looks inexpensive on trailing earnings and dividend, but forward earnings are under pressure and free-cash conversion is capex-heavy.
documents.investment_thesis:
For a value investor, MEGP presents a classic **cash-generative, asset-heavy franchise at a discount**: recurring vending revenue under long-term site contracts, net-cash balance sheet, and a shareholder-return policy targeting **>55% of post-tax profits** as dividends (FY2025 total dividend **8.64p**, up 9.5%). The screen passes five factor families — **cheapness, quality, dividend, GARP, and risk** — with notable model passes including Graham Enterprising, Earnings Yield, FCF Yield, Low P/E + High Yield, Buffett Quality, Economic Moat, High Dividend Yield, Dividend Growth, Magic Formula, Acquirer's Multiple, Dreman Contrarian, Composite Value, and Financial Health (15/22 total).

Business quality supports the screen: FY2025 EBITDA rose **5.4%** to **£120.4m** (margin **38.2%**), operating cash flow **£115.5m** (+8.9%), and laundry EBITDA grew **18.1%** to **£55.5m**, now **46.1%** of group EBITDA. Management cites dominant market positions, high barriers to entry, and rapid laundry payback on invested capital. The **£18m share buyback** (launched March 2026; **£4.5m** deployed by July 2026 per H1 filing) aligns capital return with the screen's dividend/cheapness signals.

However, the screen's failures are informative: **Graham Defensive** (current ratio 1.54 vs 2.0 threshold), **deep value/net-net** models (P/B 2.2), **Lynch PEG** (earnings growth −3.9%), **Piotroski F-Score 6/9**, and **Earnings Quality** (weak free-cash conversion vs earnings — FY2025 FCF **~£25.2m** after **£65.6m** capex). These reflect a business reinvesting aggressively for laundry growth rather than a distressed balance sheet, but they temper pure deep-value classification. On balance, the strong-buy signal is defensible on trailing metrics and franchise quality, with the caveat that **forward earnings are guided lower** and timing is neutral (RSI ~60, slightly below 200-day MA).

post_run_review.executive_summary: This run (2026-08-03) screened 249 names with 62 buy-tier signals (16 Strong Buy, 46 Buy) against 147 Holds and 40 Avoids, so actionable value is selective rather than market-wide. The deepest systemic weakness is ingest: mega-cap buy-tier names RIO.L, SHEL.L, and GSK.L each have 51–52 filings indexed without bodies (out of 61–71 total), and many buy-tier tickers show zero annual/interim classification despite non-zero filing counts. Scoring metadata gaps—especially FCF canonical vs `screen_ttm` divergence (HIK.L) and missing NCAV for all top candidates—create tension between headline cheapness and cash-flow or balance-sheet quality flags that memos cannot fully reconcile. Gap-fill updated three memos (FGP.L, HIK.L, MEGP.L) to “accumulate” with strong grades, but deep analysis still rates FGP.L and HIK.L as watchlist on leverage, FCF, and conversion concerns; conviction on top picks is capped at modest 49–55% with every signal only one week old. These gaps do not invalidate screening rank order but they block full sizing conviction until filing-body fetch, FCF overlay alignment, and principal-risks extraction improve.
